maria: Heads-up — ran a small holdout audit on Kleio-11B quant variants overnight. Want a quick readout before we push any routing flags to GTN.
ajay: nice, what variants did you try? int6 / int8 / fp16?
maria: int6 (llm-int6-lite), int8 (llm-int8-std), and fp16 baseline. 3k short-form QA prompts holdout + 500 regen checks.
liam: what metrics are we tracking? unit cost, p95, and any quality deltas?
maria: exactly. pulled token econ from the runtime trace, and eval from the holdout. TL;DR: int6 saves ~37% token-cost vs fp16, int8 saves ~18%. Quality drop is small but concentrated on long-context examples.
sarah: concentrated how? concrete numbers make it easier for PM/GTN.
maria: pasted short table below (rounded):

```
variant    | p50_lat(ms) | p95_lat(ms) | unit_cost($/1ktok) | exact_match_drop
fp16       | 45          | 180         | 0.012               | 0.0%
int8       | 48          | 210         | 0.0098              | -0.7%
int6       | 52          | 260         | 0.0076              | -2.8%
```

ajay: thanks — p95 tail increase for int6 is notable. Is the tail from KV cache behavior or kernel mismatch?
maria: dug into traces, it's a mix: a subset of long-context prompts (>=2k tokens) trigger repeated kernel fallback paths and larger mem pressure on int6 kernels. KV cache reuse still helps median, but long sequences spike.
liam: any eval signal on instruction-following quality vs short QA? We need to know if product routes chat vs single-turn QA differently.
maria: yes. on short QA (<256 tokens) int6 EM loss is ~0.5% vs fp16. on long-chain reasoning prompts (>1k tokens) int6 EM loss jumps to ~6%. so product-level impact depends on our traffic mix.
sarah: currently GTN routes ~12% long-context chat, but product wants to preserve quality for those. Suggest hybrid routing: prefer int6 for short-turns and int8/fp16 for long-turns.
liam: agreed. can we derive a simple routing predicate (e.g., input_tokens <= 512 => int6)?
maria: looked at offline traffic sample: using 512 cutoff would route ~74% of requests to int6 and keep 95% of long-context on int8/fp16. unit-econ improvement overall ~~25%.
bench-bot: perf-snapshot: uploaded artifacts to S3: s3://redwood-bridges/kleio11b/293401-snap.tar.gz
ops-bot: deploy-check: canary capacity available in us-west-2, 3 nodes reserved if you want to pilot.
ajay: next steps: (1) draft routing predicate for GTN (2) run a 24h canary with 5% traffic (3) capture model-quality eval drift on live queries and offline holdouts.
maria: I've got a PR with the predicate and a canary config — will link in the ticket. question: do we want to run an int6 variant with a slightly relaxed quant schedule (tune per-layer quant) to reduce long-tail regressions before canary?
liam: worth trying if low engineering overhead. but parallel approach: canary traffic -> monitor EM & p95; if EM degradation >1% on product holdouts, rollback.
sarah: also add a prompt-based holdout in the rollout pipeline that weights long-context examples by 3x so we don't miss regressions.
maria: will do both. I'll schedule a quick sync at 11:15 to confirm thresholds and automation.
ajay: :thumbsup:
liam: thanks, Maria. keep us posted.
bench-bot: ci: kleio-int6-tuned job finished — artifacts at s3://redwood-bridges/kleio11b/tuned/293401.tar.gz (size 1.1G)
maria: awesome, I'll add tuned variant to the canary matrix.
ops-bot: canary started at 2934012380, 5% traffic routed to int6 for short-turn predicate.
maria: tracking dashboards and will paste a short summary in 2h.
